title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of type 2 diabetes and renal function.

HPI
The patient is a 64-year-old individual presenting for a routine follow-up. They have a long-term history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease stage 4. The patient reports feeling stable and denies any acute symptoms or recent complications. They have been adherent to their current medication regimen and report no significant side effects.

Medication List
Metformin 500mg daily; Glipizide 5mg daily.

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Skin is intact with no visible lesions. Vital signs are stable. Heart rate and respiratory rate are within normal limits.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes: Currently managed with oral hypoglycemic therapy.
2. Chronic kidney disease stage 4: Stable at this time.

Plan
Continue current medications as prescribed. The patient will continue to monitor renal function and blood glucose levels. Follow up in three months for laboratory work and clinical evaluation.
explanations: CKD is listed under 'with' for diabetes in the Index, so the link is presumed: use the combination code E11.22.
Code also the CKD stage (N18.4) as instructed at the diabetes CKD code or separately when unrelated.
Long-term oral hypoglycemic use: add Z79.84.

distractors.why: The provider does not have to write 'due to'; 'with' presumes the link.
E11.2 is a subcategory; a 5th character is required.
The stage of CKD must be reported with N18.-.
Z79.84 captures long-term oral hypoglycemic use.
